newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The opposition Democrat, Chart Pattana and Palang Dharma parties expect to win more than 200 seats and form the next government. The bloc believes it will make such significant gains it will not need any coalition parties to form an administration. (BANGKOK POST)

- Senate Speaker Meechai Ruchuphan has proposed the nation elect the Constitution Drafting Assembly members before the November 17 elections so political reform can take clear shape. He warns political parties to "learn lessons" from the current government's mistakes, particularly those wooing former members of parliament from other factions. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thai border sources say senior hardliners of the Khmer Rouge and a number of their followers have fled into Thailand after a combined force of Cambodian government troops and Khmer Rouge defectors captured their stronghold at Samlot. They are taking refuge close to the border on the edge of Thai border provinces of Chanthaburi and Trat. (THE NATION)

- An investor linked with prominent investor Song Watcharasriroj has filed a complaint with the police, alleging Siam City Credit Finance and Securities Plc and its executives had cheated her of 100 million baht. They had refused to transfer 3.4 million shares in the Bangkok Bank of Commerce to securities companies as requested. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The financing for the construction and operation of Bangkok Mass Transit System Corporation's 23.5 kilometre elevated mass transit railway is in place and the project will commence commercial operations in 1999. (BUSINESS DAY)
